As shown in the figure, an object of mass $2\mathrm{kg}$ is subjected to a constant horizontal force $F=40\mathrm{N}$ pushing to the right on a sufficiently long inclined plane with angle $\theta=37^{\circ}$. The object starts moving upward along the inclined plane from rest. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the object and the inclined plane is 0.25. Take $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$, $\sin 37^{\circ}=0.6$, and $\cos 37^{\circ}=0.8$.

Find:
1. The magnitude of the supporting force on the object.
2. The magnitude of the sliding friction force on the object.
3. The magnitude of the object's acceleration.
4. The magnitude of the object's velocity at $t=3\mathrm{s}$.

method.method_draft: Use axes parallel and perpendicular to the inclined plane. First read the image: the block is on a plane rising to the right, the applied force F is horizontal to the right, and the acceleration is up the plane, so kinetic friction acts down the plane. From the text, use m=2 kg, F=40 N, theta=37°, mu_k=0.25, g=10, sin37=0.6, cos37=0.8. Resolve the horizontal force into components relative to the incline: F_parallel = F cos theta up the plane and F_perpendicular = F sin theta into the plane. Resolve weight: mg sin theta down the plane and mg cos theta into the plane. Perpendicular equilibrium gives N = mg cos theta + F sin theta = 20(0.8)+40(0.6)=40 N. Then f_k = mu_k N = 0.25*40=10 N. Along the plane, net force is F cos theta - mg sin theta - f_k = 40(0.8)-20(0.6)-10=10 N, so a=10/2=5 m/s^2. Since it starts from rest and acceleration is constant, v=at=5*3=15 m/s.

物块从静止开始做匀加速运动，t=3 s 时速度 v=at=5×3=15 m/s。

method.method_draft: Use horizontal and vertical Cartesian force equations instead of incline-axis equations. First read the image: the block lies on an incline rising to the right, the force F is horizontal rightward, and the block accelerates up the plane. From the text, use m=2 kg, F=40 N, theta=37°, mu_k=0.25, g=10, sin37=0.6, cos37=0.8. Express the acceleration components as a_x=a cos theta and a_y=a sin theta because motion is constrained along the plane. Express the normal force components as N_x=-N sin theta and N_y=N cos theta. Since the block slides upward, friction has components f_x=-f cos theta and f_y=-f sin theta, with f=mu_k N. Write Newton's second law in x and y: 40 - N sin theta - f cos theta = m a cos theta, and N cos theta - mg - f sin theta = m a sin theta. Substitute f=0.25N and the given trig values, then solve the two equations for N and a: N=40 N and a=5 m/s^2, hence f=10 N. Finally, with v0=0 and constant a, compute v(3)=a t=15 m/s.
method.CoT_raw:
先描述图像：图中物块放在一个向右上方倾斜的斜面上，斜面与水平虚线的夹角标为 θ。物块旁有一个水平向右的力 F，另有一个沿斜面向右上方的加速度 a 箭头，表示物块沿斜面向上运动。

再推理：取水平向右为 x 轴正方向，竖直向上为 y 轴正方向。已知 m=2 kg，F=40 N，θ=37°，μ_k=0.25，g=10 m/s²，sin37°=0.6，cos37°=0.8。由于物块沿斜面向上加速，设沿斜面的加速度大小为 a，则加速度分量为 a_x=a cosθ，a_y=a sinθ。支持力 N 垂直斜面，分量为 N_x=-N sinθ，N_y=N cosθ。滑动摩擦力方向沿斜面向下，大小 f=μ_k N，分量为 f_x=-f cosθ，f_y=-f sinθ。

列水平和竖直方向牛顿第二定律：
40 - N sinθ - f cosθ = m a cosθ
N cosθ - mg - f sinθ = m a sinθ
代入 f=0.25N、sinθ=0.6、cosθ=0.8、m=2、mg=20：
40 - 0.6N - 0.25N×0.8 = 2a×0.8
即 40 - 0.8N = 1.6a。
竖直方向：
0.8N - 20 - 0.25N×0.6 = 2a×0.6
即 0.65N - 20 = 1.2a。
由第一式 a = 25 - 0.5N。代入第二式：
0.65N - 20 = 1.2(25 - 0.5N) = 30 - 0.6N
所以 1.25N = 50，N=40 N。
因此 f=0.25N=10 N，且 a=25-0.5×40=5 m/s²。
物体从静止开始做匀加速运动，t=3 s 时速度 v=at=5×3=15 m/s。

因此 f=0.25N=10 N，且 a=25-0.5×40=5 m/s²。
物体从静止开始做匀加速运动，t=3 s 时速度 v=at=5×3=15 m/s。

raw_record.original_question:
As shown in the figure, an object of mass $2\mathrm{kg}$ is subjected to a constant horizontal force $F=40\mathrm{N}$ pushing to the right on a sufficiently long inclined plane with angle $\theta=37^{\circ}$. The object starts moving upward along the inclined plane from rest. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the object and the inclined plane is 0.25. Take $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$, $\sin 37^{\circ}=0.6$, and $\cos 37^{\circ}=0.8$.

Find:
1. The magnitude of the supporting force on the object.
2. The magnitude of the sliding friction force on the object.
3. The magnitude of the object's acceleration.
4. The magnitude of the object's velocity at $t=3\mathrm{s}$.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the attached figure, the inclined plane slopes upward to the right, and the block is placed on the inclined plane; the bottom of the inclined plane is marked with angle θ; there is a horizontal rightward force F on the block; there is also an acceleration arrow a, whose direction is along the inclined plane upward to the right, indicating that the block moves upward along the inclined plane. Therefore, the direction of kinetic friction should be downward along the inclined plane.

Reasoning: Take the direction along the inclined plane and the direction perpendicular to the inclined plane as the coordinate axes. It is known that m=2 kg, F=40 N, θ=37°, μ_k=0.25, g=10 m/s^2, sin37°=0.6, cos37°=0.8. The magnitude of gravity mg=20 N.

Decomposition of the horizontal force F: the component upward along the inclined plane is F cosθ=40×0.8=32 N; the component perpendicular to the inclined plane pressing into the inclined plane is F sinθ=40×0.6=24 N.

Decomposition of gravity: the component downward along the inclined plane is mg sinθ=20×0.6=12 N; the component perpendicular to the inclined plane pressing into the inclined plane is mg cosθ=20×0.8=16 N.

There is no acceleration in the direction perpendicular to the inclined plane, so the normal force N=mg cosθ+F sinθ=16+24=40 N.

The magnitude of kinetic friction f_k=μ_k N=0.25×40=10 N.

The net force along the inclined plane is F cosθ-mg sinθ-f_k=32-12-10=10 N, so the acceleration a=F_net/m=10/2=5 m/s^2.

The block starts from rest and undergoes uniformly accelerated motion, and at t=3 s the velocity v=at=5×3=15 m/s.
